questions.q: What is the key difference between Data Loader's default SOAP API and Bulk API?
options: SOAP only works for exports; Bulk API only works for inserts
Bulk API is an asynchronous, parallel-processing API built for larger batches and scale
There is no functional difference — Bulk API is just a renamed SOAP API
Bulk API requires a separate paid license
questions.explain: SOAP is synchronous and capped at 200 records per batch. Bulk API is asynchronous, processes in parallel, and supports batches up to 10,000 records.

questions.q: Where do you enable Bulk API in Data Loader, and which operations does it affect?
options: A per-job toggle that only affects Export
The Settings dialog's Use Bulk API checkbox, which affects every operation until unchecked
It's enabled automatically for files over 1,000 rows with no manual setting
A command-line flag only, never available in the desktop UI
questions.explain: Checking Use Bulk API in Settings applies to Insert, Update, Upsert, Delete, and Hard Delete alike, and stays on until you turn it back off.

questions.q: What happens to a blank CSV cell during an update when Bulk API is enabled?
options: It's treated the same as under SOAP — the field is cleared to null
It throws an error and fails the row
It's ignored, leaving the existing value in place — #N/A is needed to explicitly null the field
It automatically inserts the field's default value
questions.explain: With Bulk API on, a blank cell is simply skipped. To explicitly clear a field to null, the CSV must use the literal value #N/A.

questions.q: Which permission becomes relevant specifically because of Bulk API?
options: Modify All Data
Bulk API Hard Delete
View All Data
API Enabled
questions.explain: Hard Delete is greyed out until the Bulk API Hard Delete permission is granted — it's specifically tied to using Bulk API to permanently remove records.

questions.q: What does "Enable serial mode for Bulk API" trade away, and why would an admin choose it?
options: It trades speed for avoiding database contention on objects with heavy automation
It disables Bulk API entirely while leaving the checkbox checked
It increases the per-batch record limit beyond 10,000
It has no practical effect and exists only for legacy compatibility
questions.explain: Serial mode processes batches one at a time instead of in parallel. It's slower, but it avoids the record-locking contention that parallel writes can cause on heavily automated objects.
